TL;DR

The CLI prints semantic diffs to stdout in human-readable mode when JSON output is disabled. For YAML input, `yamlNestedScalar` reads `metadata.name` from the file text via `yamlLineValue`, and `yamlLineValue`/`yamlUnquote` strip comments and quotes but do not neutralize control characters. That value is stored in `Entity.Name` by `yamlEntity`, copied into `EntityChange.Name` by `addedChange`/`removedChange`, and then rendered into the text report. At the sink, `textStyles.render` either wraps the untrusted value in ANSI color codes or returns it unchanged; in both cases embedded ESC/control bytes are passed through to terminal output. A repository under attacker control can therefore inject terminal escape sequences into the CLI's semantic diff output.

Show more

How do I fix it?

AutoFix

Neutralize C0/C1 control characters before writing attacker-controlled strings to terminal-oriented output. A practical fix is to escape or visibly quote control bytes in `textStyles.render` (or in a shared output helper) for all human-readable fields derived from repository content, rather than printing raw values.

## Already fixed — stale findings, just retest/close

**1. RCE: "Repository-controlled file paths reach shell execution in VERIFY build checks"** (High, *PR Open*)

I checked every other `Command:` construction in that file — all paths go through `shellQuote`/`shellQuotePath`; the one unquoted concat (`"make "+target`, `:1181`) draws from a fixed allowlist `{test, check, tests}`. No open PR exists (`gh pr list` is empty), so the "PR Open" status is stale.

**8. actions/checkout persists Git credentials** (Low)
Fixed by 47606b9. All four `actions/checkout@v6` steps in `.github/workflows/test.yml` carry `persist-credentials: false`. Aikido is citing line 57; the file has moved on.

## Not real — false positives at the rule level

**2. "Possible command injection via shell script"** (High, 4 sub-findings) — **all four wrong.**
- `internal/cli/verify.go:193` — `sh -c` runs `flags.Test`/`flags.Setup`, i.e. the string the operator typed at `--test`. That's the verb's entire contract, not injection. The one path where a *derived* string reached it was finding #1, now quoted.
- `cmd/graph-bench/main.go:326`, `internal/gitutil/git.go:764`, `git.go:330` — all `exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...)`. Go doesn't spawn a shell for argv exec, so there's nothing to inject into. I also checked `git grep` for *argument* injection: patterns are passed as `-e <pattern>` with `-F` (`git.go:313-317`), so a `-`-leading query can't become a flag.

**3. "Potential file inclusion attack via reading file"** (High, 9 sub-findings) — **not real as filed.**
The rule assumes a server taking a path from a request. Every cited read takes its path from the operator: `--repo` (`ignore.go:125/137/182`), `--cache-dir` (`search_cache.go:775/793/848`), the `ENTIRE_SEARCH_SESSION` env var (`search_session.go:156`), the local transcripts dir (`stats.go:535`). `filedigest.go:69` is a generic helper with no source at all. #88 already confined the cache reads to an `os.Root` boundary.

One residual is worth naming even though I'd still not fix it: `gitInfoExcludePath` (`ignore.go:113-145`) follows a scanned repo's `.git` file → `gitdir:` → `commondir` chain, so a hostile repo can redirect that read to an arbitrary absolute path. But the bytes are only parsed as ignore rules and never printed — errors carry the path, not the content — so there's no disclosure primitive. Ignore-with-justification rather than fix.

## Real, and they share one root cause

Six findings (#4, #5a, #5b, #6, #7, #9) are all the same bug: **repository-derived bytes reach terminal-oriented output with no C0/C1 neutralization anywhere in the codebase.** I grepped for it — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go is `text.go:158` *emitting* color, and there is no `QuoteToGraphic`/`QuoteToASCII`/strip helper at all. Every sink Aikido cites is exactly where it says:

| # | Sink | Untrusted source |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `internal/cli/root.go:809` — `line += " file=" + event.Path` | Git filename via `git diff -z` |
| 9 | `internal/sem/search_outline.go:192` — `Fprintf(&buffer, "  %s", outline.FilePath)` | Git filename |
| 4 | `internal/sem/text.go:153-159` — `render()` wraps value in ANSI | YAML `metadata.name` |
| 6 | `internal/cli/search.go:918` — `Fprintf(out, "  %s\n", entry.Decl)` | verbatim source line |
| 5a | `internal/cli/search.go:851` — prints `result.Snippet` | verbatim source |
| 5b | `internal/cli/symbolref.go:713` — `Fprintf(out, "  %*d→ %s\n", …, line)` | verbatim source |

They're not equally worth fixing, though, and I'd split them:

**Fix properly (#7, #9, #4, and the path/name half of #6).** Filenames and entity names are *metadata* — no legitimate one contains ESC, so escaping costs nothing and loses nothing. #4 is the sharpest of these: `render()` concatenates the untrusted name *between* ANSI codes, so an attacker can close the sequence and take over the line. `strconv.QuoteToGraphic` on paths and names is the whole fix.

**Fix narrowly (#5a, #5b, #6's `Decl`).** These print source code verbatim, which is the product. Blanket `%q` would mangle every legitimate snippet. The right treatment is stripping/visibly-escaping only ESC and other C0/C1 (keeping tab), not quoting.

Worth noting the threat model is slightly better than Aikido frames it: the primary consumer of `--format text` here is a coding agent, not a human terminal — but an agent reading attacker-controlled bytes is its own concern, and the same bytes are in the files it would read anyway. "Low" is right; this isn't urgent, but the metadata half is cheap enough that there's no reason not to.

Closes six Aikido findings that are all the same bug, and leaves the other seven alone on purpose (triage below).

## The bug

Every human-readable renderer prints bytes a scanned repository controls: pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets. Nothing in the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go was `text.go` *emitting* colour, and there was no `QuoteToGraphic`/strip helper anywhere. A Git pathname may hold any byte but NUL and `/`, and a source file may hold any byte at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal and was interpreted rather than displayed.

| Aikido finding | Sink |
|---|---|
| Terminal escape injection via raw Git filenames in `--progress` stderr | `internal/cli/root.go` |
| Terminal control-sequence injection in text file-outline output | `internal/sem/search_outline.go` |
| Terminal escape injection in semantic diff output | `internal/sem/text.go` |
| Terminal escape/control-sequence injection via unescaped type-card declarations | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| ANSI control-sequence injection in text search output | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| CLI emits repository-controlled terminal escape sequences in source excerpts | `internal/cli/symbolref.go` |

## The fix

**The guard goes at the writer, not at each print site.** Paths and source text are printed from roughly forty places across the search, def, impact, neighbors and callsite renderers, and auditing them once would only hold until the next renderer landed. `internal/termsafe` wraps a renderer's writer so a new print site cannot reintroduce the hole — it cannot reach the terminal without passing through the escape.

Two sinks can't be covered by a wrap and are escaped by value:

- **`textStyles.render`** — this renderer emits its own ANSI codes, and the untrusted value sits *between* them. An embedded ESC there doesn't merely inject a sequence; it terminates the styling this renderer opened and leaves the terminal in a state the trailing reset was never going to close. Escaped ahead of both the coloured and the uncoloured path, since returning the value untouched when colour is off was the other half of the same hole.
- **the `--progress` line** — stderr also carries the progress bar's own cursor control, which a wrap could not tell apart from an injected sequence.

**`termsafe.Line` is the stricter variant** for values in a one-record-per-line layout. Escaping ESC alone isn't enough there: a repository can name a file `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` and print a ranked hit the search never returned. The writer can't make that call — by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte — so header fields are escaped where the renderer still knows which is which. (The `--progress` regression test caught this; the first cut of the patch let it through.)

## What does not change

**Ordinary output is byte-identical.** LF and TAB pass, and so does CR followed by LF — snippet lines are split on LF alone, so a CRLF-authored file carries its CR into every printed line. This matters beyond tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, and a snippet this rewrote would no longer match the file it came from. A *lone* CR is escaped, being exactly how a line already read gets overwritten.

**JSON and NDJSON are untouched.** `encoding/json` already escapes control characters inside strings, so no raw byte reaches those streams, and a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

`mise run check` (fmt, vet, race tests, statusline, build) passes. Regression tests: `internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go` for the rules, plus one test per reported sink in `internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go` and `internal/sem/text_escape_test.go`, each asserting the value is *defanged, not dropped*, alongside compatibility tests pinning clean output.

Yes — 457 lines across three files, 19 test functions.

**`internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go`** — the rules. A 14-case table (ESC, OSC, BEL/backspace, DEL, NUL, C1 in two-byte UTF-8, lone CR vs. CRLF, tabs/newlines, multi-byte runes) driven through all three entry points, since a rule holding for `String` but not `Writer` would be a hole. Plus `Line`'s stricter behaviour, idempotence, error passthrough, and chunked writes across the stateless boundary.

**`internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go`** — one regression test per reported sink, each driving the renderer that owns it: search text (snippet + path), type-card declaration, file outline, agent format, `def` source excerpt, and the `--progress` line. Each asserts the value is *defanged, not dropped* — silently swallowing a hostile filename would hide the file the reader is being warned about.

**`internal/sem/text_escape_test.go`** — the diff renderer, both colour off and colour on. The colour case walks every surviving ESC and requires it to be an SGR sequence this renderer emitted itself, which is the part that actually matters there: the untrusted value sits *between* our own codes.

Two of them are worth calling out because they came from failures rather than foresight:

- `TestDiffProgressLineEscapesGitFilename` failed on my first cut. Escaping ESC alone left `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` able to forge a whole ranked entry — that failure is why `termsafe.Line` exists at all. `TestSearchTextPathCannotForgeAResultLine` pins the same property for the search headers.
- Three compatibility tests (`...WithoutControlBytesIsUnchanged`, `...IsByteIdentical`) assert clean output is untouched. That's not tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, so a snippet the renderer rewrote would stop matching its file.

One gap worth naming: the sink tests are unit-level and missed `def`'s body section, which writes through `writeSymbolMatchBodies` rather than its own wrapped writer. What caught that was the end-to-end sweep against a repo with a live erase-line sequence in both a filename and a source comment. That sweep isn't in the test suite — it was manual. If you want it as a permanent guard, an integration test that builds such a repo in `t.TempDir()` and greps every text/agent verb for a raw `0x1b` would cover the class properly. ## 1. The integration sweep — `internal/cli/termsafe_verbs_test.go`

Builds a repo in `t.TempDir()` whose **filename and function body** both carry a live erase-line sequence, then drives eleven real verb invocations through `Run(...)` and fails on a raw ESC in stdout or stderr. It also pins the inverse: `--format json` must still report the exact pathname bytes Git gave us.

I checked it isn't a vacuous guard by removing each protection one at a time and confirming the sweep goes red:

| Guard | Subtests failing without it |
|---|---|
| `writeTextSearch` wrap | 1 |
| `writeAgentSearch` wrap | 1 |
| `writeDefText` wrap | 2 |

| `writeAgentNeighborsFull` wrap | 2 |
| `textStyles.render` escape | 2 |
| `writeSymbolMatchBodies` wrap | 2 |

That last row is a real limit, not an oversight. Per-file progress events are throttled to one per second and forced only every hundredth file (`sem/analyze.go:57,92`), so a fixture this size never emits a `file=` line — the subtest was passing on stdout content while looking like it covered stderr. I've documented that in the test rather than engineering a fragile 101-file fixture; that sink keeps its own unit test.

Two things worth flagging about the process: my first fixture put the escape in a comment *above* `Merge`, which no body-printing renderer emits, so the negative check came back green and told me nothing. And my first negative-check harness deleted lines in a way that broke the build — four guards reported "0 failures" that were really compile errors. Both fixed before the numbers above.

## 2. Review — one real finding, fixed

**The auxiliary search blocks could still forge lines.** `RenderSearchClosedSet`, `RenderSearchLiteralCluster` and `RenderSearchContainerMap` are one-record-per-line, but only had the writer-level guard — which stops a control sequence and *cannot* stop a newline, since by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte. ### Findings

**1. `internal/cli/explain.go:194` — high. The `explain` verb still leaks raw ESC to stdout.**
`RenderExplain` output goes straight to `opts.Stdout` with no `termsafe.NewWriter` wrap and no `Line` escaping, while it prints `symbol.FilePath` (a raw Git pathname, explain.go:296) and `symbol.Signature` (a declaration line lifted from source, explain.go:306). The new sweep `TestNoVerbLeaksControlSequencesToTheTerminal` (termsafe_verbs_test.go:68) does not list `explain`, so nothing catches it. Fix: `out := termsafe.NewWriter(opts.Stdout)` at explain.go:194 (plus `termsafe.Line` on the one-line fields), and add `explain` to the sweep.

**2. `internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:164` — medium. Escaping all of C0 rewrites form feeds in legitimate source, breaking verbatim edit anchors.**
`case character < 0x20 || character == 0x7f` escapes FF (0x0c) and VT (0x0b), which are ordinary page separators in GNU-style C, Emacs Lisp and older Perl/Python sources — not a spoofing primitive (FF just advances the terminal). Verified: a `lib.c` with `\f` page breaks now renders its search snippet as the literal 4-byte `\x0c`. That contradicts the package doc's own invariant ("ordinary output stays BYTE-IDENTICAL … so an agent can copy a snippet verbatim as an edit anchor") — an agent copying that snippet as an `old_string` anchor will fail to match the file, and `TestSearchTextWithoutControlBytesIsUnchanged` uses only clean ASCII so it does not catch this. **3. `internal/sem/search_verify.go:1231` — medium. The VERIFY block's `targets` line is not `Line`-escaped, so a pathname newline forges a line inside the payload.**

## The bug

Every human-readable renderer prints bytes a scanned repository controls: pathnames from `git diff -z`, entity names parsed out of YAML, whole source lines lifted verbatim into snippets. Nothing in the codebase neutralized terminal control characters on the way out — the only `\x1b` in non-test Go was `text.go` *emitting* colour, and there was no `QuoteToGraphic`/strip helper anywhere. A Git pathname may hold any byte but NUL and `/`, and a source file may hold any byte at all, so an ESC in a filename or a declaration reached the reader's terminal and was interpreted rather than displayed.

| Aikido finding | Sink |
|---|---|
| Terminal escape injection via raw Git filenames in `--progress` stderr | `internal/cli/root.go` |
| Terminal control-sequence injection in text file-outline output | `internal/sem/search_outline.go` |
| Terminal escape injection in semantic diff output | `internal/sem/text.go` |
| Terminal escape/control-sequence injection via unescaped type-card declarations | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| ANSI control-sequence injection in text search output | `internal/cli/search.go` |
| CLI emits repository-controlled terminal escape sequences in source excerpts | `internal/cli/symbolref.go` |

## The fix

**The guard goes at the writer, not at each print site.** Paths and source text are printed from roughly forty places across the search, def, impact, neighbors and callsite renderers, and auditing them once would only hold until the next renderer landed. `internal/termsafe` wraps a renderer's writer so a new print site cannot reintroduce the hole.

Sinks that a wrap cannot cover are escaped by value: `textStyles.render` (this renderer emits its own ANSI codes and the untrusted value sits *between* them, so an embedded ESC terminates styling we opened), the `--progress` line (stderr also carries the progress bar's cursor control), and `RenderExplain` (its byte budget is measured on the strings it builds).

**`termsafe.Line` is the stricter variant** for one-record-per-line layouts. Escaping ESC alone isn't enough there: a repository can name a file `a.go\n1. src/real.go:1 score=99.0` and print a ranked hit the search never returned. The writer can't make that call — by then a snippet's newline and a path's are the same byte.

## What does not change

**Ordinary output is byte-identical.** LF, TAB, FF and VT pass, and so does CR followed by LF. This matters beyond tidiness: agents copy printed snippets verbatim as `old_string` edit anchors, and a snippet the renderer rewrote would stop matching its file. (Form feeds are page separators in GNU-style C and Emacs Lisp — an early version of this PR escaped them and broke exactly that invariant.) A *lone* CR is escaped, being how a line already read gets overwritten.

**JSON and NDJSON are untouched.** `encoding/json` already escapes control characters inside strings, and a consumer of the machine formats is entitled to the exact bytes Git reported.

## Verification

`mise run check` (fmt, vet, race tests, statusline, build) passes.

Unit tests: `internal/termsafe/termsafe_test.go` for the rules; one test per sink in `internal/cli/termsafe_sinks_test.go`, `internal/sem/text_escape_test.go` and `internal/sem/search_blocks_escape_test.go`, each asserting the value is *defanged, not dropped*, plus compatibility tests pinning clean output.

The sweep is what caught `def` writing its body section through `writeSymbolMatchBodies` rather than its own wrapped writer, which the per-renderer tests had missed.

## The review's findings, verified and fixed

**1. `explain` was leaking outright** (the serious one). `RenderExplain` prints a Git pathname and a signature lifted from source, and `runExplain` wrote it straight to stdout with no guard. Escaped by value rather than by wrapping, because its byte budget is measured on the strings it builds.

**2. Escaping all of C0 broke form feeds** — a compatibility regression I introduced. `\f` is an ordinary page separator in GNU-style C, Emacs Lisp and older Perl; a snippet of such a file was rendering it as a literal `\x0c`. That violates the invariant this package exists to protect, since agents copy snippets verbatim as edit anchors. FF and VT now pass in keep-layout mode — neither is a cursor primitive, a terminal treats both as an index — while `Line` still escapes them.

**3. The VERIFY block forged lines.** `targets`, `derived_from` and `guarded by` concatenated paths raw, so a file named `evil.go\n99. real.go:1 score=99.0` split the record. Execution was never at risk (the path is shell-quoted), but VERIFY is the line an agent is told to *run* — the worst place to leave the display open. It rendered as a clean single line after the fix.

**4. Siblings skipped my own rule** — including `agentSearchTypeCard`, the direct `--format agent` twin of the text type card I had escaped in the same hunk. **5. `termsafe.String` was dead code** whose doc pointed at a caller that had moved to `Line` — an invitation to pick the wrong variant. Removed.

Plus the one I found myself before the review returned: the closed-set, literal-cluster and container-map blocks had only the writer-level guard.

Every guard is negative-checked — removed, then confirmed the suite goes red. That process caught three of my own harness bugs, worth flagging because two of them initially produced *false all-clear* results: deleting lines that broke the build (reported as "0 failures"), and a `replace(...,1)` that reverted the text type card instead of the agent one, so the agent test passed while looking like it proved coverage.

content.text:
Codex found seven issues. All seven were real — including one it proved by running my test in a way I hadn't.

## The one that mattered most: my sweep was wrong

Codex ran `env -u NO_COLOR FORCE_COLOR=1 go test ...` and it **failed**. The sweep asserts "no ESC in stdout", but the diff renderer emits its *own* SGR sequences when colour is on. It passed for me only because `NO_COLOR=1` happens to be set in my shell — so the test would have broken for any developer or CI job without it. Colour is now pinned off in the sweep, which is what makes it test one property: that nothing the *repository* supplied reaches the terminal as a control sequence. The coloured path keeps its own test. Both suites now pass with forced colour on and off.

That's a good catch about my verification method, not just the code.

## Two design-level findings

**Stray 8-bit C1 bytes weren't escaped.** My C1 branch only recognised the two-byte UTF-8 form (`0xc2 0x9b`), but a Git pathname is a byte string — a raw `0x9b` arrives on its own, and an 8-bit-locale terminal reads it as CSI. My package doc claimed C1 coverage, so this was a real gap in a stated contract.

Fixing it safely required making the scan UTF-8 aware rather than per-byte, which is the interesting part: the middle byte of `日` (U+65E5 = `e6 97 a5`) is `0x97`, squarely inside the C1 range. A naive check would have mangled every CJK identifier in the codebase. `escapedAt` now returns the *width* of the sequence it judged so both scan and rewrite step over valid runes instead of reading their interiors. Stray bytes above `0x9f` are deliberately left alone — not controls in any encoding, and rewriting them would corrupt Latin-1 sources.

**My VERIFY fix broke the VERIFY contract.** Escaping the rendered command made the line safe but left a command that no longer names the file it came from — and "runnable as written" is that field's documented contract. Codex was right that I'd traded one defect for another. The fix belongs in the deriver, not the renderer: a command built around a control-byte path can't be both runnable and printable, so it isn't emitted. The existing residual floor already says "nothing derivable here", which is the truthful answer. Confirmed end-to-end — the hostile repo now gets `VERIFY: none derivable` instead of a command that would target a nonexistent file.

## Five more sinks of the class I'd already been fixing

`formatCallSiteLocation` (names the call site, so it doesn't delegate to the function I *did* fix), `disambiguationSelectors` (where a forged newline also offers a `--file` argument that isn't the file), `agentDiagnosticPath` and the shared completeness renderer (subject is an unparseable file, printed *ahead* of the ranking), `defRelatedLine`, and the impact co-change entries.

Worth noting the pattern: three consecutive reviews each found more instances of the same one-line-record class. That's a sign the writer-level guard doesn't compose with per-field escaping as cleanly as I claimed — the wrap can't distinguish a path's newline from a snippet's, so every new one-line field is a fresh opportunity to forget. A stronger design would make one-line rendering a type rather than a convention. I haven't done that; it's a larger refactor than this PR should carry, but it's the honest read on why the tail keeps producing findings.

All six new guards negative-checked (removed, confirmed red). `mise run check` green. Five commits on the branch; PR #96's description still reflects the previous round, so it's now one round stale — say the word and I'll refresh it.
